podcast.body: A song from 1899, cited as an early example of a rhythm similar to the "Bo Diddley beat," illustrating that such foundational rhythms have long existed and are not copyrightable. "We have to go back to 1899 for a song by Charles Hale called at a dark town cakewalk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song from 1899 is referenced as a historical precedent for certain rhythms, predating the "Bo Diddley beat" and demonstrating that rhythmic patterns have a long history of shared usage. "We have to go back to 1899 for a song by Charles Hale called at a dark town cakewalk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
